description: Implement the Android :app module wiring the Phase 1 user features on top of :core, with the HYBRID transport so it works both on the same Wi-Fi AND when the phone is remote. Includes: pairing UI (show/scan QR + short code), a foreground SyncService that maintains the relay WebSocket connection and also runs LAN NSD discovery + direct socket when peers are on the same network, Universal Clipboard (read/write clipboard and sync sealed text), screenshot capture via MediaProjection and file/photo sharing (send sealed file metadata + chunks), and a minimal Compose UI (paired devices list, last received clipboard, received-files inbox). NOTE: this module requires the Android SDK which is NOT present in the sandbox, so it is validated by structural/code review and by relying on :core (already unit-tested). The user builds/runs it in Android Studio; verification steps for them live in docs/VERIFICATION.md.
steps: Create app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml with permissions: INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, ACCESS_WIFI_STATE, CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE (for NSD), FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC, POST_NOTIFICATIONS; declare the SyncService (foreground, dataSync) and the MediaProjection permission flow. targetSdk 34.

Create app/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/app/transport/RelayClient.kt: a ktor OkHttp WebSocket client that connects to the configured relay URL, sends Hello(deviceId, pairingId), receives Envelopes and emits them via a Flow, and sends sealed Envelopes. Auto-reconnect with backoff so a device that roams/sleeps re-establishes (supports remote operation).

Create app/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/app/transport/LanTransport.kt: NsdManager registration + discovery of the _linkup._tcp service on the LAN and a ServerSocket/Socket pair using :core Framing to exchange the SAME sealed Envelopes directly, bypassing the relay when peers are local. Provide a TransportRouter that prefers LAN when a peer is discovered and falls back to relay otherwise, exposing one send(Envelope)/incoming Flow regardless of path.

Create app/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/app/pairing/ a PairingManager storing pairing secrets/link keys in EncryptedSharedPreferences (androidx.security-crypto), QR generation (zxing) + a camera scanner screen, and short-code entry; on pair, derive the link key via :core E2E.deriveLinkKey and persist PairedDevice.

Create app/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/app/clipboard/ClipboardSync.kt: read local clipboard (ClipboardManager) on a user-triggered 'send' action (document the Android 10+ background clipboard-access restriction and that reading requires foreground/an explicit action), seal the text via :core EnvelopeCodec and send; on receiving a CLIPBOARD_TEXT envelope, open it and offer/paste to the local clipboard with a notification.

Create app/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/app/share/ScreenshotCapture.kt (MediaProjection request + capture to PNG) and FileShare.kt (SAF document picker + chunked sealed FileChunkPayload send; reassemble incoming chunks, verify sha256, save to app storage / MediaStore). Wire a share-target so other apps can push files in.

Create app/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/app/service/SyncService.kt: a foreground service holding TransportRouter + RelayClient alive, showing a persistent notification, and dispatching incoming envelopes to clipboard/file handlers. Start on boot/app-open.

Create a minimal Jetpack Compose UI under app/src/main/kotlin/com/linkup/app/ui/: MainActivity + screens for Devices (list paired devices + Add via QR/code), Clipboard (show last received, 'Send current clipboard' button), and Inbox (received files/screenshots). Keep it functional, not polished.

Add app/src/main/res (strings, launcher icon placeholder, notification channel strings) and a BuildConfig/relay URL config field (default to a placeholder the user replaces with their deployed :relay host).
acceptance_criteria: All :app Kotlin references :core public APIs that exist (EnvelopeCodec, E2E, Pairing, models) with correct signatures (compile-consistency verifiable by review; full compile needs the SDK).
TransportRouter exposes a single send(Envelope)/incoming Flow and documents LAN-preferred-with-relay-fallback so the app works whether the phone is near (same Wi-Fi) or far (mobile data via relay).
AndroidManifest declares the foreground SyncService and all permissions needed for NSD, foreground sync, notifications, and media projection.
Pairing secrets are stored encrypted (EncryptedSharedPreferences), and link keys are derived via :core, never hardcoded.
Code review confirms the app sends/receives the SAME sealed Envelope type over both transports (no plaintext over the relay).
verification: Structural review: run `./gradlew projects` to confirm :app still configures (SDK-permitting); the coder MUST NOT fail the feature if `:app:assembleDebug` is impossible due to the missing Android SDK, but MUST record that limitation in the feature findings.
Run `grep -rn "com.linkup.core" app/src/main` to confirm :app uses the shared, tested core protocol/crypto.

Confirm docs/VERIFICATION.md lists the on-device steps (install on 2+ devices, pair, copy text on one and paste on another on the same Wi-Fi AND on mobile data via deployed relay, take a screenshot and confirm it arrives).
findings:
REVIEW FIX (2026-10-02, review 071415): (#1 screenshot foreground-service type) AndroidManifest now requests FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION and declares SyncService as android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync|mediaProjection"; capture is driven via SyncService.captureScreenshot(), which elevates the running foreground service to include FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_MEDIA_PROJECTION for the duration of the capture then restores dataSync-only. SyncService.onBind now returns a LocalBinder so an in-process Activity can invoke the capture while the typed service is foreground. This removes the SecurityException on API 29+/34. (#2 bidirectional pairing) Added app/pairing/PairingHandshake.kt: the QR scanner calls announceToInitiator() after acceptPairing() to send a sealed PAIRING_HELLO (its own DeviceInfo) to the initiator; SyncService dispatches PAIRING_HELLO to PairingHandshake.onEnvelope(), which records the peer via new PairingManager.recordPeer(). PairingManager.selfDeviceInfo() helper added. DevicesScreen wires announce on both scan and paste-payload paths. (#3 concurrent transfers) FileShare now delegates reassembly to the unit-tested :core FileReassembler keyed on pairingId:transferId and tags every meta+chunk with a fresh UUID transferId; removed the old 'first in-flight transfer' attribution and local InboundTransfer/sha256 code. (#4 short code) Removed the cosmetic generateShortCode() status text and relabeled the input field to 'Paste pairing payload'; DevicesScreen docs note Phase 1 has no relay-side pending-pairing index. (#5 relay client bound to one pairing) RelayClient now multiplexes one WebSocket per pairing id (connect() launches a reconnect loop per pairing; send() routes by Envelope.pairingId); SyncService and LinkupContainer pass pairedDevices().map{pairingId}.distinct(). Kept a single-pairing convenience constructor. (#6 double-delivery) TransportRouter now dedups inbound envelopes on (fromDeviceId, pairingId, nonceB64) via a bounded LinkedHashMap so the LAN<->relay fallback cannot double-apply clipboard/notify; a legitimate re-send uses a fresh nonce and is not deduped. VERIFICATION: :app cannot be assembled (no Android SDK); validated by code review + the fixed logic living in the :core FileReassembler/PairingHelloPayload which ARE unit-tested (./gradlew :core:test green). ./gradlew projects configures all three modules. --- ORIGINAL: Implemented the full Android :app module on top of the already-tested :core, committed as 60887ce.

WHAT WAS BUILT (all paths under app/src/main):
- AndroidManifest.xml: added INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, ACCESS_WIFI_STATE, CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC, POST_NOTIFICATIONS; declared SyncService (foregroundServiceType=dataSync, exported=false); added a SEND share-target intent-filter on MainActivity; launcher icon + @string/app_name.
- transport/RelayClient.kt: Ktor 2.3.12 OkHttp WebSocket client. Sends the relay's exact Hello shape {"deviceId","pairingId"} as the first frame, emits received Envelopes via a SharedFlow, send() writes sealed Envelope JSON, connect() auto-reconnects with capped exponential backoff (1s->30s) so a roaming/sleeping phone re-establishes (the FAR path).
- transport/LanTransport.kt: NsdManager register+discover of _linkup._tcp, ServerSocket accept loop + client Socket using :core Framing.readFrame/writeFrame to exchange the SAME sealed Envelopes directly (the NEAR path).
- transport/TransportRouter.kt: the single send(Envelope)/incoming Flow surface. Prefers LAN when a peer is discovered (lan.hasPeer), falls back to the relay otherwise, with cross-fallback on delivery failure. Merges both transports' incoming flows.
- pairing/PairingManager.kt: stores pairing secrets + stable deviceId in EncryptedSharedPreferences (AES256_SIV/AES256_GCM via MasterKey/Keystore). Link keys are NEVER stored; derived on demand via :core E2E.deriveLinkKey. createPairing/acceptPairing use :core Pairing + persist PairedDevice. pairing/QrCodec.kt generates the QR bitmap via zxing core; DevicesScreen scans via zxing-android-embedded ScanContract.
- clipboard/ClipboardSync.kt: sendCurrentClipboard() reads ClipboardManager on explicit user action and seals via :core EnvelopeCodec; onEnvelope() opens CLIPBOARD_TEXT and sets the local clip. Documents the Android 10+ (API 29) background clipboard-read restriction in code + UI.
- share/FileShare.kt: SAF/share-target bytes -> sealed FileMetaPayload then chunked FileChunkPayload (256KiB, under Framing's 16MiB cap); receiver reassembles, verifies sha256, saves via MediaStore (images) or app files (other). share/ScreenshotCapture.kt: MediaProjection consent intent -> one-shot VirtualDisplay+ImageReader -> PNG -> FileShare.sendBytes(kind=SCREENSHOT).
- service/SyncService.kt: foreground dataSync service owning TransportRouter+RelayClient, persistent notification channel, dispatches incoming envelopes by kind to clipboard/file handlers.
- ui/: single-activity Compose MainActivity + Devices/Clipboard/Inbox screens + a tiny LinkupContainer service-locator so UI and service share one PairingManager (one encrypted store, stable deviceId) and one router. Starts SyncService on open; requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS on 13+.
- res/: strings (incl. notification channel), colors, adaptive launcher icon placeholder.
- app/build.gradle.kts: enabled buildConfig; added buildConfigField RELAY_URL default "wss://relay.linkup.example/ws" (placeholder the user replaces with their deployed :relay). Added catalog + deps: androidx.security:security-crypto 1.1.0-alpha06, com.google.zxing:core 3.5.3, com.journeyapps:zxing-android-embedded 4.3.0 (ktor-client-okhttp/websockets were already present).
- docs/VERIFICATION.md: JVM/sandbox steps + on-device steps for pairing and testing clipboard/screenshot/file on same Wi-Fi (LAN) AND on mobile data via the deployed relay (far-away phone).

:core API usage was matched exactly against core/src/main (EnvelopeCodec.sealEnvelope/openEnvelope, E2E.deriveLinkKey, Pairing.*/PairingPayload, Envelope + ClipboardPayload/FileMetaPayload/FileChunkPayload toJson/fromJson, WireJson, DeviceInfo/DeviceType/PairedDevice/TransferKind). grep shows 29 com.linkup.core references across 11 app files.

SDK LIMITATION (expected, not a blocker): there is NO Android SDK in the sandbox, so `:app:assembleDebug`, lint, and instrumentation tests CANNOT run here and were intentionally not attempted. The :app module is validated by structural/code review plus the already-passing :core it builds on. The user compiles/runs :app in Android Studio (API 26+). Minor runtime note for the user: zxing-android-embedded's CaptureActivity expects an AppCompat/Material theme at runtime; swap the placeholder Theme.Linkup if the scanner activity needs it.

VERIFICATION RUN IN SANDBOX: `./gradlew projects` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL (all three modules, including :app, configure with the new catalog/deps). `./gradlew :core:test :relay:test --rerun-tasks` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL (JVM modules unaffected). grep for com.linkup.core in app/src/main confirms the app uses the shared tested core.
